text_blocks.snippet: The Families First Coronavirus Response Act (FFCRA) is a federal law enacted in the United States on March 18, 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The FFCRA aimed to provide financial assistance and support to individuals and businesses impacted by the pandemic, particularly those who were unable to work due to COVID-19.

list.title: Paid Sick Leave:
list.snippet: Employees were entitled to up to 80 hours of paid sick leave for reasons related to COVID-19, including illness, quarantine, or caring for a sick family member.

list.title: Emergency Family and Medical Leave:
list.snippet: Employees were eligible for up to 12 weeks of paid leave for reasons related to COVID-19, such as caring for a child whose school or daycare was closed or caring for a sick family member.

list.title: Unemployment Benefits:
list.snippet: Extended unemployment benefits were provided to individuals who lost their jobs due to COVID-19.

list.title: Food Assistance:
list.snippet: Increased funding was allocated to food assistance programs, such as SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program).

list.title: Testing and Contact Tracing:
list.snippet: Funding was provided for COVID-19 testing and contact tracing efforts.

text_blocks.snippet: Most provisions of the FFCRA expired on December 31, 2021. However, some provisions, such as the expansion of unemployment benefits, were extended through September 3, 2023.

list.snippet: The FFCRA was enacted as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act.
For more information on the specific provisions and implementation of the FFCRA, refer to the official government sources.
